payload.source_label: The real scalar constant-coefficient equation is hyperbolic

contract.statement: For any real constant scalar A, the one-dimensional scalar equation q_t + A q_x = 0 is hyperbolic [raw PDF p.23, printed p.1, equation (1.1) and scalar-specialization paragraph]. Here hyperbolicity is the surrounding matrix criterion requiring real eigenvalues and a full linearly independent family of eigenvectors, specialized to one component [raw PDF p.25, printed p.3, first paragraph].
assumptions: The equation belongs to the homogeneous first-order constant-coefficient linear class q_t + A q_x = 0 in one spatial dimension [raw PDF p.23, printed p.1, equation (1.1) and enclosing paragraph].
There is exactly one dependent component, m = 1, so A is a scalar, and that scalar is real [raw PDF p.23, printed p.1, scalar-specialization paragraph].

Hyperbolicity classifies the system through its coefficient A; the selected passage imposes no particular initial profile or chosen solution q [raw PDF p.23, printed p.1, scalar-specialization paragraph; raw PDF p.25, printed p.3, defining criterion for A].
The advection equation and translated-profile formula follow as examples and do not form part of the selected assertion [raw PDF p.23, printed p.1, equations (1.2)–(1.3)].
quantifiers: An arbitrary constant real scalar coefficient A, obtained by specializing the coefficient matrix of (1.1) to m = 1 [raw PDF p.23, printed p.1, scalar-specialization paragraph].
The background independent variables are x and t in R, and the unknown q takes values in R^m, specialized to one component [raw PDF p.23, printed p.1, equation (1.1) and following paragraph].
